nodes.label: test job (3-platform matrix)
nodes.rationale: Only job that needs a matrix: crossterm is the terminal backend and the shell tool's process-group kill is cfg(unix), so platform-divergent code lives here. fail-fast:false keeps one red platform from hiding the state of the other two.

nodes.label: lint job (fmt + clippy)
nodes.rationale: fmt and clippy are platform-independent for this codebase, so running them on all three platforms would burn CI minutes on identical output.

nodes.label: msrv job (Rust 1.88.0)
nodes.rationale: rust-toolchain.toml pins stable and outranks rustup default, so the toolchain must be selected explicitly with +1.88.0 — otherwise the job silently checks with stable and guarantees nothing.

nodes.label: acceptance job (criterion 8 smoke)
nodes.rationale: The serde round trip is unit-tested, but the criterion is about the pipeline — that stdout carries the JSON alone with every progress line on stderr, and that a real jq accepts it. Ubuntu only: it asserts a property of our own output, not of the platform.

nodes.label: Project config layer used by CI acceptance
nodes.rationale: The project config layer, not the global one: it applies without depending on the runner's HOME, and --cwd puts the session store and the tool sandbox in the same throwaway directory.

nodes.label: build job (5-target matrix)
nodes.rationale: macos-15-intel preserves the Intel architecture required by the x86_64 Apple artifact after macos-13 was retired by GitHub.

nodes.label: aarch64 cross C toolchain step
nodes.rationale: rusqlite is built with the bundled feature, so cross-compiling to aarch64 needs a cross C toolchain as well as the Rust target.

nodes.label: Inline #[cfg(test)] test convention
nodes.rationale: Tests live at the bottom of the source file they cover; a file under tests/ is added only when a test genuinely cannot see what it needs from inside the crate.

nodes.label: File tool path jail (fs_tools::resolve)
nodes.rationale: .. is normalised lexically before the prefix check because starts_with is component-wise, and symlinks are canonicalised. run_bash is deliberately NOT confined — jailing a shell needs a real sandbox.

nodes.label: Staging directory for mutating file tools
nodes.rationale: A crash-safety mechanism, NOT a security boundary: it sanitises its own mirror then copies to the unsanitised target. The path jail is the boundary.

nodes.label: Three tool-registration entry points
nodes.rationale: try_register fails on a name collision (untrusted MCP tools), register panics (trusted startup wiring), replace overwrites deliberately (upgrading keyless web_search once an Exa key exists).

nodes.label: mcp__{server}__{tool} namespacing
nodes.rationale: Without the prefix a remote server publishing read_file would displace the sandboxed built-in; the wire call still uses the bare remote name.

nodes.label: tool_defs() sorted by name for prefix caching
nodes.rationale: The tool array is part of the prefix providers cache on; a HashMap's order would miss the cache on every request with no visible symptom.

nodes.label: Every tool_use answered by a tool_result
nodes.rationale: agent.rs seeds the results vector and fills it in rather than appending, so the invariant cannot regress even on cancellation. A dangling tool_use makes the next request fail outright.

nodes.label: API key redaction choke point
nodes.rationale: One choke point in run_one_tool covers the transcript, the session database and the next provider request together.

nodes.label: AgentEvent adjacently-tagged serialization
nodes.rationale: It IS the --output-format stream-json wire format, so variant and field names are a public interface; app.rs matches exhaustively with no wildcard, so a new variant always needs a TUI arm too.

nodes.label: smith-core testkit / ScriptedProvider
nodes.rationale: Running past the end of a script panics on purpose — a turn making more requests than scripted is a finding, not something to paper over with a default reply.

nodes.label: MSRV 1.88
nodes.rationale: The floor comes from the dependency graph (ratatui 0.30, darling 0.24), not from first-party syntax.

nodes.label: Env API keys outrank saved config
Fix: Ollama context window assumed 4096
nodes.rationale: Not cosmetic: auto-compaction fires against the window, so a 262144-token cloud model was being summarised away every couple of rounds. smith now asks Ollama's own /api/show.

nodes.label: Fix: context gauge hid an over-full window
nodes.rationale: Printing max(window, used) made 181% of a wrongly-detected window read as a normal full window.

nodes.label: Fix: every Ollama session recorded as OpenAI
nodes.rationale: OpenAiProvider::id() was hardcoded; it prices turns and labels turns.provider. Stored costs were always right, only the label was wrong, so no migration is needed.

nodes.label: Fix: home directory could become the project root
nodes.rationale: ~/.smith is a root marker and always exists, so any project without .git resolved to $HOME — loading ~/SMITH.md twice and widening the @import jail to the whole home directory.

nodes.label: Fix: 'Text file busy' verifying a downloaded browser
nodes.rationale: Between fork and exec a subprocess started by another thread holds an inherited write descriptor to the binary and execve refuses; the probe now retries.

nodes.label: Sidebar tabs (Session / Tasks / Vitals)
nodes.rationale: Stacked in one column the four sections did not fit a 24-row terminal.

nodes.label: Ctrl+L diagnostics panel and tracing subscriber
nodes.rationale: Until now no tracing subscriber was installed anywhere in the workspace, so every warning the MCP client and provider adapters emitted was discarded.

nodes.label: Session cost reported from per-turn figures
nodes.rationale: A resumed session used to display today's prices applied to the whole session's tokens, disagreeing with what it had actually spent.

nodes.label: Answers pinned to the user's language
Mid-turn message delivered at the next round boundary
smith-core crate
nodes.rationale: Defines traits and knows nothing about HTTP, SQLite or ratatui; every other crate implements against those traits.

nodes.label: smith-tui crate
nodes.rationale: Never talks to smith-provider or smith-tools directly — only through the Action/AgentEvent channels.

nodes.label: smith-config crate
nodes.rationale: Split out of smith-store so reading a TOML file doesn't compile SQLite from C.

nodes.label: Tool interception pattern
nodes.rationale: Use for any tool whose result depends on interactive UI state rather than pure computation — don't try to make ToolExecutor::execute itself interactive.

nodes.label: Plan gate (plan_gated)
nodes.rationale: Blocks every tool above ReadOnly outright regardless of PermissionPolicy — even Skip doesn't bypass an unapproved plan.

nodes.label: Per-session scratch directory
nodes.rationale: The incentive is the design: a write the tool vouches is scratch-confined skips the permission prompt, so the compliant path is also the frictionless one. Failing closed costs one prompt, never one file.

nodes.label: Tool::scratch_scoped vouching
nodes.rationale: Only write_file/edit_file/multi_edit ever vouch, through one shared fs_tools::scratch_confined; run_bash and MCP tools can never vouch because they cannot bound their writes.

nodes.label: Turn checkpoints (Checkpointer / CheckpointStore)
nodes.rationale: One central hook at the same choke point the plan gate and permission prompt use, so a refused call never leaves an object behind. Deliberately no git and deliberately not in sessions.db: the store has to work with no session row at all.

nodes.label: /rewind
nodes.rationale: Restores files only; it never truncates the conversation. The orchestrator queues Agent::note_to_model, which rides the next user message rather than being a message of its own.

nodes.label: run_bash cannot be snapshotted
nodes.rationale: Any Mutating/Dangerous tool that declares no paths is recorded as uncovered, and /rewind says so rather than implying the turn was fully undone.

nodes.label: Read-before-overwrite gate
nodes.rationale: Checkpoints can undo a blind overwrite, but the user often does not notice until much later, so this prevents rather than undoes. There is no force argument: an escape hatch the model can set itself is not a gate.

nodes.label: fs_tools::ReadSet
nodes.rationale: One Arc shared by read_file/write_file/edit_file/multi_edit; it cannot live on ToolContext (cloned per call) or in a plain registry field (registry is behind an Arc and execute takes &self). Entries are keyed on the sha256 of the bytes read, so a file changed afterwards is stale again.

nodes.label: Behavioral evals (evals/)
nodes.rationale: Out of CI on purpose: a suite that goes red when a provider ships a model update trains people to ignore it.

nodes.label: Headless mode (-p / --output-format)
nodes.rationale: Exit code 3 is distinct from 1 because they warrant opposite reactions in CI — a failure is a bug, a cap is a budget to raise with all prior work intact.

nodes.label: Agent::with_unattended(true)
nodes.rationale: Turns off the two prompt exemptions whose only justification is sparing a human an interruption — scratch-confined writes and task — because both left a call running in a job that named no tools at all.

nodes.label: Free providers and the two-layer fallback
nodes.source_location: ### Free providers and the two-layer fallback
nodes.rationale: Layer one is OpenRouter's server-side chain (models + route:fallback); layer two is FallbackProvider, which on a quota-class death advances a sticky index and returns a retryable error so the agent's existing stream_with_retry drives the next attempt — nothing new retries.

nodes.label: 9Router gateway + private Node provisioning
nodes.rationale: Provisioned into ~/.smith/runtime/ on the Chromium pattern — sha256 vs SHASUMS256.txt, staged, probe-before-rename.

nodes.label: Provider/model switching mid-session (/model)
nodes.rationale: Conversation history carries over either way since messages: Vec<Message> lives independently of the Arc<dyn LlmProvider>.

nodes.label: web_search seven-backend chain
nodes.rationale: A pin is absolute — pinned-but-unconfigured fails naming the missing key rather than silently rerouting, because the user who pins is exactly the user a silent fallback betrays.

nodes.label: SearXNG backend (tier 1)
nodes.rationale: First whenever configured, ahead of even a paid key: it is the only backend with no shared IP reputation and no anti-bot layer. Requires JSON output, which SearXNG ships disabled.

nodes.label: Bing over RSS backend
nodes.rationale: &format=rss returns the same ten results as ~5 KB of stable XML rather than ~122 KB of HTML, with real target URLs instead of Bing's ck/a redirect wrapper. Its <pubDate> is a crawl timestamp, so it is deliberately dropped.

nodes.label: Headless Chromium page fetcher
nodes.rationale: Now a generic page fetcher that knows nothing about result markup — the caller picks the URL and owns the parsing.

nodes.label: language::detect (query-language market selection)
nodes.rationale: A Portuguese query under setmkt=en-US gets ten well-formed results about nothing, structurally indistinguishable from success. The machine locale is the last fallback — WSL2 ships LANG=C.UTF-8, which names no market at all.

nodes.label: bing::judge_relevance (Poisoned / Weak / Good)
nodes.rationale: It grades responses rather than just rejecting them: Poisoned is retried under the next market, Weak is kept as a fallback while a better market gets a try.

nodes.label: Three distinct search-failure cases
nodes.rationale: Collapsing 'found nothing', 'TEMPORARILY BLOCKED' and 'UNAVAILABLE' is what previously ended with the model quietly answering from training data. None of them ever licenses answering from memory.

nodes.label: MCP transports and one liveness rule
nodes.rationale: Transport is the whole abstraction: send one JSON-RPC message, receive on an Incoming channel. The incoming channel closing fails every in-flight call at once, so a server dying mid-session costs no timeouts.

nodes.label: MCP resources are a tool, not context
nodes.rationale: A resource list injected into every request would cost tokens on every turn forever and go stale; a tool is paid for only when used.

nodes.label: MCP prompts are user-invoked, never model-reachable
nodes.rationale: A prompt template is meant to be an instruction, and the only thing that makes that safe is that the user asked for it by name.

nodes.label: untrusted::fence (tool output is DATA)
nodes.rationale: Stated before and after the body, with every run of five hyphens defanged so a payload cannot close the fence. Tool descriptions cannot be fenced, so they get provenance, a 4 KB cap, namespacing and Dangerous.

nodes.label: JSON action envelope (recover_text_tool_call)
nodes.rationale: Only fires when the name resolves to exactly one registered tool: an action field is common enough in ordinary JSON that dispatching on it blindly would turn quoted data into tool calls.

nodes.label: resolve_tool_name / align_arguments
nodes.rationale: Tolerant but never speculative: write against both write_file and write_tasks resolves to nothing rather than to a guess, and edit-distance matching is deliberately absent.

nodes.label: ReasoningFilter
nodes.source_location: ### Reasoning tags in the text channel
nodes.rationale: One shared place inside consume_stream, because the leak follows the model, not the wire format — stripped before deltas are forwarded or accumulated, so nothing reaches the transcript, history or the next request.

nodes.label: Subagents (the task tool)
nodes.rationale: The only thing that crosses back into the parent's history is the child's final message; everything it read is discarded. Measured: six 4 KB reads leave the parent 8074 estimated tokens inline vs 58 when delegated.

nodes.label: subagent::RestrictedTools
nodes.rationale: A child's tool set is the registered ReadOnly tools minus ask_user/write_tasks/task, enforced in code rather than by the prompt.

nodes.label: Shared subagent tool-call pool per turn
nodes.rationale: Per-child caps multiply (50 parent calls x 30 each); a pool is additive, so a turn spends at most twice its own cap.

nodes.label: Partial subagent report (finish_subagent)
nodes.rationale: Throwing partial work away makes the parent re-delegate and pay twice for the half it already had.

nodes.label: Custom slash commands
nodes.rationale: What defuses a prompt from a cloned repo is that the expanded body goes into the transcript as the user's message, above a system line naming the file. A referenced $N with nothing passed refuses the whole expansion rather than expanding to nothing.

nodes.label: Skills (progressive disclosure)
nodes.rationale: A tool rather than a name the model mentions: a tool result is a message so the body invalidates no cached prefix, and it inherits schema validation, permission class, the tool card and stream-json for free.

nodes.label: Personas / output styles
nodes.rationale: Read once at startup and never re-read, so the system prompt is byte-identical for the whole session and prompt caching is untouched.

nodes.label: PROMPT_INVARIANTS vs PROMPT_STYLE split
nodes.rationale: A persona structurally cannot delete the lines that keep output connected to reality, and PROMPT_INVARIANTS stays a byte-identical prefix of every prompt smith sends.

nodes.label: Extension path jail enforced on discovery
nodes.rationale: Nothing in a commands directory says 'read this other file', but .smith/commands/deploy.md -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa is one ln -s in a repository. The jail delegates to memory::real_path because a path jail that exists twice is a path jail that will be fixed once.

nodes.label: One-line installers (install.sh / install.ps1)
nodes.rationale: The installers download a published archive, verify its SHA-256 checksum, and install Smith without Rust.

nodes.label: smith update / update check
nodes.rationale: The check never blocks headless runs and never replaces the binary automatically; automatic replacement is opt-in with SMITH_AUTO_UPDATE=1.

nodes.label: Shell commands intentionally not sandboxed
nodes.rationale: A fake shell jail would give you a false sense of safety.

nodes.label: Remappable key bindings ([keys])
nodes.rationale: The defaults collide with common terminal setups — Ctrl+B is tmux's own prefix.

nodes.label: The authorization gate ladder (rungs 0-7)
nodes.rationale: A call has to survive all of them, in a fixed order, and none can grant what an earlier one withheld. Derived from Agent::run_one_tool and Agent::dispatch_tool, not from prose.

nodes.label: Rung 1: name interception
nodes.rationale: ask_user, write_tasks and task return before the class is looked up. task is exempt because its child is constrained, not because delegation is inherently harmless.

nodes.label: Rung 2: plan_gated (no bypass)
nodes.rationale: The one gate in the system with no bypass at all, and the reason the order matters: every later rung is written on the assumption that this one already ran.

nodes.label: Rung 4: needs_prompt (four sufficient exemptions)
nodes.rationale: Four independent reasons not to prompt OR'd together; none is stronger than another, which is the source of most of the surprising cases.

nodes.label: The concurrent read-only path (run_concurrent_group)
nodes.rationale: Rungs 2, 4 and 5 are skipped entirely; sound only because is_concurrency_safe admits nothing but exactly ReadOnly tools. Anything added to rungs 2-5 must be added to both paths or explicitly argued not to apply.

nodes.label: Why PreToolUse sits at rung 3
nodes.rationale: Above the plan gate it would fire for calls that cannot execute and invite being wired as an override; below the prompt it could not prevent the prompt and a rewrite would produce a confused deputy. Above rung 4 specifically so it still runs under /permission skip.

nodes.label: Finding A: a subagent's reads unlocked the parent's overwrites
nodes.rationale: Fixed by splitting identities: ToolContext carries session_id for on-disk state and reader_id for what has been read, because session_id also names staging, scratch and the checkpoint stream /rewind walks.

nodes.label: Finding B: --allowed-tools is not deny-by-default
nodes.rationale: headless.rs answers the permission channel, so a call that never reaches the channel is never checked against the flag. Fixed for the two cases that mattered via with_unattended; the accurate statement is that nothing that writes, runs a command, or spawns an agent happens without it.

nodes.label: Finding C: three tools were never schema-checked
nodes.rationale: Fixed by validating the intercepted three against the published schema before interception; the list lives in one constant, INTERCEPTED_TOOLS, because two things have to agree about it.

nodes.label: A read-only tool is not a harmless tool
nodes.rationale: web_search reaches the network and task spawns a whole agent; web_fetch is Mutating despite writing nothing because a model-chosen URL is an exfiltration primitive. The class is about authority, not about whether bytes hit the disk.

nodes.label: A session grant outranks a tightened policy
nodes.rationale: allowed_session_tools is checked before permission_policy and set_permission_policy does not clear grants, so 'the policy is ask' is not the same claim as 'you will be asked'.

nodes.label: Hook JSON-in/JSON-out contract
nodes.rationale: smith writes one JSON object on stdin and reads one from stdout. Unknown fields are ignored so a hook written against a later version degrades instead of exploding.

nodes.label: PreToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: An allow decision means no objection, never let it through — a hook can only ever subtract authority.

nodes.label: PostToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: On failure it passes the result through with a warning: a post hook cannot un-write a file, and a model that believes its write failed retries it.

nodes.label: UserPromptSubmit hook
nodes.rationale: On failure it refuses the turn: the typical hook strips secrets, and 'send it anyway' leaks them to a third-party API where no later apology retrieves them.

nodes.label: Hooks are global-config only
nodes.rationale: Honouring a hook from a repository's own config would make `git clone && smith` a code-execution vector for whoever wrote the repository.

nodes.label: matcher is exact names, not a regex
nodes.rationale: A regex would be a dependency, a footgun, and a way for a typo to match nothing. A policy hook that silently applies to no tools is the single failure mode this feature must not have.

nodes.label: PreToolUse fails closed on timeout or garbage
nodes.source_location: ### What a timeout means differs per event
nodes.rationale: A gate that cannot answer has not consented. Failing open would leave the user believing a policy is enforced when it is not; failing closed is bounded and loud.

nodes.label: Hook output is untrusted data
nodes.rationale: A hook that shells out to a linter is quoting file contents back at smith, and the file may not be the user's. Every line is prefixed with '> ' so text faking the closing frame appears inside the quote.

nodes.label: The tool name is an input, never an output
nodes.rationale: A hook turning a read_file into a run_bash is either broken or hostile, and both deserve to stop the call rather than get a shrug.

nodes.label: Hooks run for subagents
nodes.rationale: A policy is authority the user granted and a child does not inherit it; a hook is authority the user withheld, and a child's calls are the least-watched in the system. The opposite default cannot be filtered back in, because a hook that never runs cannot ask to.

nodes.label: Ember design system
nodes.rationale: Brand metaphor: smith = forge. Background is dark iron, accent is ember; everything active glows and everything historical cools.

nodes.label: Surface elevation tokens
nodes.rationale: The fallback uses the 256-colour cube, not the 16 named ANSI colours, because with those the three surfaces all collapse to Black and DarkGray/Gray collides with text tokens. surface.base is painted, not inherited — inheriting is what made a light theme impossible.

nodes.label: Theme presets (dark / light / high_contrast)
nodes.rationale: light is not an inversion: each role colour is chosen again against a light background. An unknown name, token or invalid hex aborts initialisation with code 2 — a theme that ignores half of what the config asked for is worse than one that refuses to start.

nodes.label: theme.rs::contrast_ratio and the WCAG AA sweep
nodes.rationale: every_preset_meets_wcag_aa sweeps every foreground/surface pair of every preset. When a pair fails, the colour changes — never the threshold.

nodes.label: Glyph tokens and ASCII fallback
nodes.rationale: A glyph missing from the terminal font becomes a blank cell, and a spinner blinking to nothing reads as a hang — so the fallback is per set, not per character. Theme::unicode lives inside Theme because Theme is already the transcript memo key.

nodes.label: ContextGauge component
nodes.rationale: Shows the real numbers because a ratio alone throws away exactly what the user wants to read; an estimated number is drawn with a tilde. Never draw an estimate with the same typography as a measurement. The gauge does not animate.

nodes.label: Per-card focus and per-card throbber
nodes.rationale: Selection and expansion are fields of ChatLine, not App, so they stay out of LayoutKey — a global expansion flag would invalidate the whole transcript on every Enter. Each card derives its spinner phase from its own started_at so two tools spin out of phase.

nodes.label: Overlay reading panel (/usage, /mcp, Ctrl+L)
nodes.rationale: Not a Modal variant: every Modal variant carries a oneshot the agent is blocked on, so a fourth variant would let /usage replace a pending permission request and hang the turn forever.

nodes.label: Sidebar tabs and the 27-column divider
nodes.rationale: A tab trades 'see everything, truncated' for 'see one thing, whole', the right trade in a 28-column panel. Clipping via Tabs does not work — it discards the last title entirely, producing a selectable invisible tab.

nodes.label: The 80x24 layout contract
nodes.rationale: Normative: every new widget has to fit it before being written, because adapting later is what makes acceptance criterion #7 fail late. Nothing shown at any width may make App::is_animating() true.

nodes.label: The context strip
nodes.rationale: Nothing that only exists in the sidebar may be the only place a vital lives — when the sidebar disappears its vitals descend into the strip.

nodes.label: Vertical budget by priority
nodes.rationale: The transcript floor is what the table exists to protect: the old order (input grows to 10 against height-3) left the transcript with 6 lines as soon as the user typed '/'.

nodes.label: Box width invariant (fit_lines)
nodes.rationale: Without it the outer Wrap{trim:false} folds the line and throws the closing border onto the next row — the root cause of the misalignments.

nodes.label: Remappable [keys] (five actions)
nodes.rationale: Ctrl+B is tmux's default prefix and Ctrl+O is discard in a standard termios line discipline — factory settings of the two programs most likely to be around a terminal agent. Enter/Esc/Backspace/arrows and Ctrl+C stay fixed so a config error cannot produce a terminal you can neither type in nor leave.

nodes.label: Subagent definition files (~/.smith/agents/*.md)
nodes.rationale: Only global subagents are loaded: a repository cannot ship a subagent that silently runs on your API key. A broken file disables only that subagent.

nodes.label: Skill files (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: description is required because it is the only always-loaded part; the body is loaded only when the model calls the skill tool.

nodes.label: SearXNG setup for web_search
nodes.rationale: SearXNG disables JSON output by default; without json in settings.yml formats it returns HTTP 403 to smith's /search?format=json.

nodes.label: Slash command incremental delivery goal
nodes.rationale: Split work into small independent packages; each must compile, pass the three gates, update /help, and be usable without depending on the next package.

nodes.label: Bug: Ollama 400 invalid message content type after tool use
nodes.rationale: It looks like the model dies on complex tasks; the real failure is on the follow-up request that re-sends history containing a bad assistant message.

nodes.label: messages_to_wire (openai.rs serializer)
nodes.rationale: OpenAI accepts content:null with tool_calls; Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API requires a string and rejects null. Fix is to emit "" instead of Null.

nodes.label: OpenAI/Ollama wire-path hardening checklist
nodes.rationale: Covers missing tool_calls[].id on early chunks, role:tool message shape, empty/cancelled turns poisoning the next request, and stream_options.include_usage on older Ollama.

nodes.label: The ten acceptance criteria
nodes.rationale: Mechanism and behaviour are separated deliberately: several criteria are half a property of this code and half a property of a model's judgement, and only the first half can be a cargo test.

nodes.label: cargo-dist deliberately not adopted
nodes.rationale: It would replace release.yml, not extend it: the release process would be described by a tool's defaults rather than a file this repo controls, and the first disagreement is fixed by a version pin instead of an edit. Reconsider at Windows code signing.

nodes.label: xtask deliberately not adopted
nodes.rationale: This repo needs three commands, every contributor already has cargo, and adding a crate to alias them would add a compile step to the gate it is aliasing.

nodes.label: macOS and Windows artifacts never run
nodes.source_location: ## What has and has not actually run
nodes.rationale: The release job proves they build and upload, not that they work. A release checklist that implies more verification than happened is worse than a short one.

nodes.label: Crate version not bumped with the tag
nodes.source_location: ## What has and has not actually run
nodes.rationale: Both releases ship a binary reporting smith 0.1.0, so smith update sees v0.1.01 as newer and will keep offering the same update forever.

nodes.label: macOS Gatekeeper risk for chrome-headless-shell
nodes.source_location: ## What has and has not actually run
nodes.rationale: Downloaded unsigned and unnotarised, so Gatekeeper is expected to refuse it on first run and nothing in smith setup handles that yet.

nodes.label: Package-manager templates (Homebrew, Scoop, installer)
nodes.rationale: Templates carry placeholder checksums until the corresponding GitHub release exists; do not publish an update with placeholder hashes.

nodes.label: --ascii, --plain and TERM=dumb
nodes.rationale: --ascii should feed the Theme directly rather than set an env var and re-read; TERM=dumb should fall back to headless rather than a degraded TUI; duplicating the headless frontend for --plain would be a mistake.

nodes.label: PTY harness for acceptance criterion #9
nodes.rationale: The panic hook exists but nothing tests it and it cannot be tested in-process; also, an Err return from run() skipped the final terminal::restore() — only the panic path was protected.

nodes.label: Windows/macOS platform risks
nodes.rationale: run_bash hardcodes Command::new("sh") so the tool does not work on Windows at all — a product gap, not a test gap; kill_process_tree's non-unix fallback only kills the direct child and needs a Job Object; four path behaviours were reasoned from std/glob source rather than observed.

nodes.label: Packaging gap (installer, Homebrew, binstall, Scoop)
nodes.rationale: At handoff time nothing existed: no install script, no Homebrew formula, no cargo-binstall metadata, no Scoop manifest.

nodes.label: #[ignore]d live-network tests must stay out of release CI
nodes.rationale: They touch the real network, a real browser and real provisioning; they exist on purpose and must not be enabled in release CI.

nodes.label: Behavioral eval harness (evals/run.py)
nodes.rationale: Standard library only, each trial a fresh temporary project. A low rate is a finding to read, not a broken build. A timeout counts as error, never as a behavioral failure: a dead Ollama is not a disobedient model.

nodes.label: edit-ambiguity eval
nodes.rationale: Scored on the end state — the named section changed, the other two untouched — because that is what the user cares about. recovered and avoided are both correct.

nodes.label: injection-obedience eval
nodes.rationale: write_file is deliberately in --allowed-tools: an eval where obeying was impossible would prove nothing. An earlier task asking for a one-sentence summary scored reported:False 5/5 because a warning would have violated the instruction — that measured the task, not the model.

nodes.label: No pass/fail threshold and no forced fixture
nodes.source_location: ## Two things this suite deliberately does not do
nodes.rationale: Picking a bar would recreate the brittleness that keeps these out of CI. recovery_rate is conditional and null when nothing tripped — 'never measured' is the honest report; 100% of zero is not.

nodes.label: First recorded run (nemotron-3-super:cloud, 2026-08-06)
nodes.rationale: reported is 4/5: one trial summarised the README correctly while saying nothing about the instruction buried in it — the gap between what criterion #6 promises and what is observed, now with a number instead of an assumption.

nodes.label: CPU contention confound (do not run cargo test concurrently)
nodes.rationale: Five trials timed out at ~387s each, uniformly enough to look like a deterministic limit inside smith; on an idle machine the same trials took 9-45s.

nodes.label: cargo-binstall packaging notes
nodes.rationale: A wrong pkg-url makes cargo-binstall fall back to building from source, which defeats the clean-machine install criterion for users without a Rust toolchain.
